q: The van Kampen theorem computes the fundamental group of a space X = U ∪ V (U,V open, path-connected, with U∩V path-connected) as:
opts: The free product π₁(U) * π₁(V) modulo the normal subgroup generated by i_U(γ)i_V(γ)⁻¹ for γ ∈ π₁(U∩V)
exp: Seifert-van Kampen theorem: π₁(X) is the pushout of π₁(U) and π₁(V) over π₁(U∩V)—the amalgamated free product. This is the main computational tool for fundamental groups: e.g. π₁(S¹) = ℤ, π₁(figure-eight) = F₂.
